ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: A pond has two populations, zooplankton and algae, and the trends in their population densities over time are shown in the figure. If a large number of a certain kind of fish (C) that specializes in eating zooplankton are released into the pond, after a period of time, only one population remains among the three populations A, B, and C in the pond. What is the relationship between A and B?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A pond has two populations, zooplankton and algae, and the trends in their population densities over time are shown in the figure. If a large number of a certain kind of fish (C) that specializes in eating zooplankton are released into the pond, after a period of time, only one population remains among the three populations A, B, and C in the pond. What is the relationship between A and B?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is "population density" and the horizontal axis is "time". A is labeled as the solid line, and B is labeled as the dashed line; both curves show periodic fluctuations, and the peaks and troughs are staggered. It can be seen that in several cycles, when A is at a high level and then begins to decline, B continues to rise from a lower level and subsequently reaches a higher level, and the changes in their numbers show a mutually restricting, phase-shifted relationship. Reasoning: The stem limits the original two populations to only zooplankton and algae. Algae are producers, and zooplankton feed on algae; the introduced fish C specializes in eating zooplankton. If after a period of time only one population remains among A, B, and C, then the one that can remain alone in the long term should be algae, because fish cannot survive alone without zooplankton as food, and zooplankton also cannot survive without algae. Combined with the phase relationship in the figure, where B rises after A declines, this can be explained as B recovering after the grazing pressure on it is reduced when A decreases. Therefore B corresponds to algae, and A corresponds to zooplankton that feed on algae. Thus the relationship between A and B is predation, and A preys on B.
